verification: Opened exact theorem and class-C definition. Compactification of divergent automorphisms assumes Fujiki class C; this is explicitly unavailable in the filling problem, so no compactness conclusion is imported.

locator: Theorem 3 and opening proof, journal p.511
verification: Reduced parameter space and constant h0 yield the local isomorphism property for families pointwise isomorphic on the entire base. Punctured-base agreement alone does not meet the premise.

Opened the full multivariable fan construction: positive semidefinite symmetric forms with positive definite sum, periodic fan and flat fan map; arbitrary period twists are symmetric. PUSH invokes its related polarized construction only, and proves its nonsymmetric analytic quotient independently.

Properness is exactly inverse-image equality of fan supports. Applied on each finite fan over an original affine chart; analytification of this proper algebraic toric map gives the local analytic modification. No finite-type conclusion is asserted for the whole infinite fan before quotient.

Opened all goodness conditions and the explicit distinction in 9.2: log de Rham comparison (i) needs no projectivity under log-smooth-base/exact hypotheses, whereas Hodge filtration and log Hodge structure need further conditions. The present non-Kähler filling is not classified by the full log Picard theorem.

locator: Theorem 1.1 and Section 2, equations (1)–(10), manuscript pp.1–5
verification: Parabolic Inoue surface with b2=m>0, identity automorphisms C*, explicit infinite toric atlas and deck action. For m=8 the central scaling action fixes the elliptic curve and has reciprocal weights at the eight cycle nodes; the paper separately derives its vector-field/cohomology calculation.

Simple normal crossing complex surface with at most double curves, dual normal bundles, anticanonical conductors and matching opposite residues. Conclusion is a smooth real total space with continuously varying complex structures off the double locus, expressly weaker than a holomorphic smoothing. It cannot supply the required proper holomorphic family.

Opened exact classification alternatives and explicit elliptic Hopf component glued to an elliptic K3 along a smooth fibre. Supports existence of non-Kähler components in analytic semistable degenerations only; no Kähler component hypothesis may be inferred merely from properness.

locator: Definition of degeneration, p.1; Theorem 3.1, p.2
verification: Semistable Kähler total space and trivial canonical bundle are explicit hypotheses of the torus degeneration classification; these are unavailable for the proposed non-Kähler caps. No classification is transferred without them.

Opened full cocycle proof of Theorem B on a Stein manifold: positive coherent cohomology vanishes. Applied to the actual locally free sheaf of vector translations on the Stein punctured-base product, not to the nonlinear torus torsor without its separate integral obstruction.

Proper algebraic stack over C has equivalent algebraic and analytic coherent-sheaf categories. The weighted projective root curve is a proper algebraic Deligne–Mumford stack; invertibility of a line bundle is local on its atlas. This supplies exactly the Picard comparison, independently also proved by the explicit analytic characters.

Opened identification of infinitesimal complex deformations with H1 of holomorphic vector fields. Used as context only: the paper prints the complete Čech coboundary-to-trivialization argument and records its sign convention.

Opened exact torus algebraic-reduction statement: quotient by a connected complex subtorus is an abelian variety realizing the algebraic reduction. Applied to a compact two-dimensional complex torus; no projectivity of the original torus is presumed.

verification: Opened fixed-torus Green critical equation and upper bound five, with the three half-period critical points. This counts critical points in the torus coordinate, not critical moduli of the composite height used here.

locator: Definitions (1.2)–(1.3), Theorem 1.1; Appendix A, (A.1)–(A.3), Propositions A.1–A.2, pp.2101–2102
verification: Opened derivative identities and complete simple-zero proof. Their eta1 is pi²E2/3, matching our normalization; their holomorphic functions f(k,C) differ from the real-analytic factor 3ZP−2g2 on wp=0. No global modulus exclusion is inferred from their theorem.

Opened multiple Green function and measure-zero exceptional moduli theorem. It supplies generic nondegeneracy of fibre-coordinate critical points, not exclusion of every critical modulus for the specific composite function.

Opened exact fixed-torus theorem: an existing nontrivial critical pair has positive Hessian. This is compared only with the first factor of the composite derivative; it does not handle its other factor or establish the present global level classification.
